applicable.principle: Let the service process carry the visual sequence when no real photography is available.
applicable.why: The synthetic brief gives an exact monthly scope and contact sequence, while the media inventory has zero usable images. The inspected Northline desktop capture shows type scale and a right-side checklist making a sparse first screen legible; mobile preserves its verbal hierarchy but the cookie notice takes substantial space.

applicable.principle: Use strong type hierarchy for the owner question, then quieter detail for scope and exclusions.
applicable.why: The inspected Northline home separates a large claim from a compact process list. Harbor Ledger needs an equally clear but distinct accounting expression without borrowing its wording or exact composition.

avoided.principle: Project-photo proof as a first-screen device
avoided.why: No client work or real team photography exists; the inspected Tide & Slate example works because its large roof image depicts work, which Harbor Ledger cannot substantiate.
Its oversized legal headline and identical right-side checklist would make the accounting site feel borrowed rather than driven by the monthly reporting process.

plannedApplication.homepage: A ledger-inspired timeline will explain capture, reconciliation, and monthly conversation; a concise first screen will state the service and honest email next step.
plannedApplication.interior: A service-scope page will expand the monthly cycle, exclusions, pricing process, and fit-call behavior without inventing client proof.

teachingPrinciples.reason: Zero real images and a documented repeatable bookkeeping scope favor process-based explanation.
The visitor needs to scan scope, exclusions, and next step without photographic proof.
